existingExamples.reason: Preserved the original function, tasks, reflection methods and vertices. Replaced sampled straight-line paths with exact segments, separated the solution sketches so coincident branches remain identifiable, explicitly associated each vertex with its part and added coordinate annotations. Plain solution prose and mathematics inherit the implemented blue styling. No relation-led continuation requires an equals gutter.

coverage.summary: Retained and formatted the existing linear comparison example; added one quadratic comparison example with different source values to cover the remaining assessed methods. Practice and quiz content was classified only, without mathematical re-audit or alteration. New working follows the supplied booklet's reflection methods. Diagram labels specify 10 pt and graph ticks 8.5 pt; actual rendering and final-size verification remain for the later visual stage. No files were written.

examples.derivation: Formatting preserves f(x)=x-2 and both original tasks. Absolute-output reflection gives y=|x-2| with vertex (2,0) and y-intercept (0,2). Absolute-input reflection gives y=|x|-2 with vertex (0,-2) and zeros x=±2. Every plotted segment agrees. The methods match source lines 864–871 and 956–963.

For f(x)=(x-2)^2-1, zeros are 1 and 3, the minimum is (2,-1), and f(0)=3. Reflecting the negative section produces local minima (1,0), (3,0) and local maximum (2,1). For f(|x|)=(|x|-2)^2-1, zeros are ±1 and ±3, minima are (±2,-1), and (0,3) is a local maximum. Both piecewise plots agree. These are changed-value adaptations of the supplied quadratic reflection tasks and instructions.

review.summary: The two examples cover all four mapped assessed methods. The existing example preserves its mathematics; the added quadratic example follows the booklet’s reflection methods within scope. Separate editable prompts and solutions, annotations, diagram colours and gutter usage are suitable. Solution prose/math inherit blue styling. Final-size typography and visual acceptance remain for the later capture stage. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited.
